description: Prototype restrictions in Defk.Compiler: branch_type! rejects array-valued branches, and returned arrays must come from alloc/2. Cause: param array views are rebound on every resume, so copies held in frame vars would go stale after GC. Needs tracking of which view a variable refers to, or rebinding of all aliases on resume.

comments.text: Also hit by examples/rolling_stats.exs (defk-9p6.1): an if returning a tuple ({s1 - old, q1 - old * old} vs {s1, q1}) is rejected ('branches returning tuples are not supported'); rewrote it as a scalar if on the leaving sample. Tuple-valued branches are a natural Elixir idiom inside reduce bodies.

Per 'Decide array value semantics' (defk-i2e): arrays have value semantics with static copy-on-write (defk-auo). When arrays flow through branches, tuples or returned inputs, the uniqueness analysis must follow them, copying conservatively where it can't prove a single live binding.

Triage (defk-sgw plan): needs-triage. Two approaches named (track which view a variable refers to, or rebind all aliases on resume) and it interacts with 'Give arrays value semantics' (defk-auo), which copies conservatively once arrays flow through branches. Pick the approach after defk-auo lands; not required for the verdict.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Arrays may be the value of if/cond/case branches, and a kernel may return an input array, correct first: copy conservatively wherever the copy analysis cannot prove a copy unnecessary

**Decision (maintainer, triage 2026-10-11):** correctness first. Tuple-valued branches of scalars already work; this is the array part. Value semantics (defk-auo) and agreement properties (defk-ne6) have landed.

**Current behavior:**
An array-valued branch is the compile error array-in-branch; returning an input array the kernel never writes is return-input-array. The original reason: input array views are rebound on every resume (the binary may move across GC), so a frame variable holding a copy of a view would go stale.

**Desired behavior:**
- `x = if c, do: a, else: b` (and cond/case, and arrays inside branch tuples) works for any mix of input arrays and owned arrays (alloc/copies) of the same element type. After a yield and resume, x refers to the right, current data: either the branch result is an owned buffer (copy an input view into an owned buffer when it flows through a branch), or the frame records which input it aliases and rebinds it on resume. Choose; the conservative copy is acceptable for a first version, and say which you chose and its cost.
- Writes through x follow value semantics: never visible through a or b, never visible to the caller's binaries.
- Returning an input array the kernel never wrote returns the caller's own binary (no copy), also inside a result tuple and from a branch.
- The copy analysis (nested/arm?/carried etc.) follows arrays through branches; when unsure it copies.
- Errors array-in-branch and return-input-array are removed or narrowed to what remains unsupported; registry and generated docs updated; docs/language.md Returning/branches sections updated.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Tests: branch between two inputs, input vs alloc, alloc vs alloc, nested branches, array in a branch tuple, write after the branch (value semantics: inputs unchanged), returning an unwritten input (same binary, e.g. :erts_debug.same/2 or binary_part referencing), returning an input from one branch and an alloc from the other
- [ ] All of the above under forced yields with a GC between resumes (input binaries large enough to be refc), and agreement (assert_agrees) properties
- [ ] Kill mid-call leaves frames_live at 0
- [ ] `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean; note in docs/performance.md if the conservative copy has a measurable cost in an example

**Out of scope:**
- Sub-array views / slice (defk-n4r.3, unblocked by this)
- Avoiding the conservative copies beyond what the existing analysis gives

Implemented on branch defk-gqk (ef40cc8), not merged. Chose rebind over copy: a branch's temporary holds the arm's view; array locals that held an input's view at a yield are re-bound at resume by pointer match against the input as saved at that yield (F->p_x). Arms' buffers merged into one alias class for the copy analysis. Unwritten input returned as the caller's own term (data+len match against inputs), else owned handover, else literal bytes copied. array-in-branch and return-input-array removed. Cost: none measurable (perf 6.26, provisional). Tests: test/array_branch_test.exs incl. forced yields + GC between resumes (heap and refc), kill mid-call, agreement properties; full suite, docs, credo clean.

title: Allow arrays through if/cond branches and returning input arrays
